content: David Nicholson, CBE, is a senior administrator within the English National Health Service (NHS). He was appointed as the Chief Executive of the NHS in September 2006. Nicholson graduated from Bristol University with a degree in History and Politics, achieving a 2:1 classification. During the 1970s, he was a member of the Communist Party and remained affiliated with it until 1983. In 1988, Nicholson became the Chief Executive of the Doncaster Royal Infirmary NHS Trust, one of the first-wave NHS Trusts. During his tenure, he introduced Clinical Directorates and led the Trust as a national pilot for Total Quality Management. In 1997, he transitioned to the Trent NHS Regional Office, where he served as the Regional Director of Performance. By November 2000, he was appointed as the Regional Director. Between December 2001 and March 2002, Nicholson took on the role of Regional Director for the former Eastern and West Midlands regions, while simultaneously maintaining his responsibilities in Trent. During this period, he also shadowed the position of Director of Health and Social Care (designate) for the Midlands and East of England. In April 2002, Nicholson formally assumed the role of Director of Health and Social Care for the Midlands and East of England. This position placed him in charge of eight Strategic Health Authorities, overseeing healthcare services for a population of 20 million people. In 2003, he was appointed Chief Executive of the Birmingham and The Black Country Strategic Health Authority (BBC SHA). By August 2005, he was asked to take on additional responsibilities as Chief Executive of the neighboring Shropshire and Staffordshire SHA, as well as the West Midlands South SHA. In April 2006, Nicholson was appointed Chief Executive of the newly established London Strategic Health Authority. This marked his fifth job change within a single year. Nicholson was recognized for his contributions to public service with a CBE in the 2004 New Year Honours list. Additionally, he received an honorary Doctor of the University award from the University of Central England in Birmingham. He is a father to two sons—one a recent graduate and the other currently studying at university. Nicholson is also an avid supporter of Nottingham Forest Football Club.
